diagnosis.message: Hello! Today we learn CSS flexbox. Have you ever tried to put three buttons in one line? How did you do it?

explain.message: Think of people standing in a queue at a ticket counter. The queue is the container, the people are the items. With display flex, the container lines up its children in a row. justify-content decides how they spread along the line. align-items decides how they line up from top to bottom. flex-wrap lets them move to the next line when space runs out. Shall we try a menu bar?
explain.mermaid:
graph LR
  container[display: flex] --> a[item] & b[item] & c[item]
  container -. justify-content .-> mainaxis[main axis]
  container -. align-items .-> crossaxis[cross axis]

example.message: A shop page has a menu with a logo, links and a cart button. Give the menu display flex, justify-content space-between and align-items center. The logo goes left, the cart goes right, and everything is centred vertically. What would happen if you add flex-wrap wrap on a phone?

another_way.message: Another way: think of plates on a long dining table. display flex is laying them in one row. justify-content is how the gaps are shared: bunched at the start, centred, or spread evenly. align-items is whether they touch the table edge or sit in the middle. Which property spreads plates evenly?
another_way.mermaid:
graph LR
  container[display: flex] --> a[item] & b[item] & c[item]
  container -. justify-content .-> mainaxis[main axis]
  container -. align-items .-> crossaxis[cross axis]

not_understood.message: Let us go step by step. First, the parent gets display flex. Now its children sit side by side. Second, justify-content moves them left, right or apart. Third, align-items moves them up, down or to the middle. Which property puts items side by side?
not_understood.mermaid:
graph LR
  container[display: flex] --> a[item] & b[item] & c[item]
  container -. justify-content .-> mainaxis[main axis]
  container -. align-items .-> crossaxis[cross axis]

doubt.answer: Good question. justify-content works along the main direction, which is a row by default. align-items works across it. If you set flex-direction column, they swap. Does that help?

code.prompt: Lay out a .menu so its items sit in one row, spread apart, centred vertically, wrapping on small screens.

questions: On a {context}, the header has a logo, three links and a button. Explain how you would use flexbox to place them in one row with even spacing.
Cards on a {context} overflow the screen on a phone. How can flexbox make them move to the next line? Explain the properties you use.
On a {context}, explain the difference between justify-content and align-items with one small example.

feedback.good: You used display flex with the right alignment properties.
feedback.missing: Explain which property works along the row and which works across it.
feedback.next: Start with display flex on the parent, then name each property and its effect.
